original_value: Quadrature spatial modulation (QSM) is one of the most prevalent transmission techniques for future wireless mobile network due to its high spectral efficiency (SE) and low complexity. However, it is restrictive to downlink of the cellular network deployments. Therefore, this paper proposes QSM for the multiuser uplink data transmission that increases the SE of the network by deploying multiple antennas at the mobile user with only two radio frequency (RF) chains. Maximum likelihood (ML) decoder is used to detect the received signal and attains the optimal detection performance but it is impractical because of its high computational complexity. Consequently, this paper proposes compressed sensing (CS) based orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) detection as it has a suboptimal performance with a low computational complexity which can be a practical solution in the high‐density uplink multiuser network. However, conventional OMP algorithm has a low estimation performance due to multiuser interference which corrupt channel matrix. Thus, this work design an equalizer that mitigates the multiuser interference and improve the detection performance by orthonormalizing the columns of channel matrix. Simulation analysis confirm that the proposed QSM technique based on CS detector outperforms the conventional schemes in terms of SE and bit error rate (BER).

result.paraphrase: Quadrature spatial modulation (QSM) is among the most widely used transmission techniques for future wireless mobile networks because of its high spectral efficiency (SE) and low complexity. However, it is limited to downlink cellular network deployments. To address this, the paper proposes QSM for multiuser uplink data transmission, boosting network SE by using multiple antennas at the mobile user with only two radio frequency (RF) chains. Maximum likelihood (ML) decoding detects the received signal and provides optimal detection performance, but its high computational complexity makes it impractical. The paper therefore proposes compressed sensing (CS)-based orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) detection, which offers suboptimal performance with low computational complexity and can serve as a practical solution for high-density uplink multiuser networks. Yet the conventional OMP algorithm suffers from poor estimation performance because multiuser interference corrupts the channel matrix. To overcome this, the work designs an equalizer that suppresses multiuser interference and improves detection performance by orthonormalizing the channel-matrix columns. Simulation results confirm that the proposed QSM technique with a CS detector outperforms conventional schemes in terms of SE and bit error rate (BER).
